en: [The Kindling of the Fire] Having washed his feet and taken up the *pavitra* grass together with *akṣata* grains, [he recites]: "May we prosper through our oblations, having approached with reverence—the Friend, the God, the Friend... Having held the *pavitra*, he offers the *akṣata* grains along with the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*) and betel leaves (*tāmbūla*). "Strengthening the Anurādhās with every oblation, may we live for a hundred autumns, blessed with heroic sons. Thus, having held the *pavitra*, he offers the *akṣata* grains, the sacrificial fee, and the betel leaves.

Salutation to Dāya-onnamaṣṭadaśa, the lord of the ten [who are] worthy of worship; salutation to the eye of those who are worthy of worship and stand before [us]; salutation to Heaven, salutation to Earth.

(4th line) (…) O Prathasabha, protect me and those who are members of the assembly and those who sit in the assembly; make them endowed with power, and grant full life-span constantly to all (5th line).
Having prostrated, saying "Salutation to the illustrious Vaiṣṇavas," [he says]: "O entire assembly, this [gift] has been offered by me at the base of your feet. (6th line)

Having accepted a golden sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), or whatever fee is prescribed, [one should say]: "May there be the attainment of fitness for me to re-establish the *aupāsana* fire, which has been interrupted for many periods, together with this my lawful wife (*dharmapatnī*); please grant your favor. The response: "So be it... may there be the attainment of fitness.

Seated upon *darbha* grass, holding *darbha* blades, having performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), [one makes] the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*): "Viṣṇu, wearing white garments, moon-colored, four-armed..."

One should meditate upon the one with a serene countenance for the pacification of all obstacles. [At the shrine] having as its support the elephant-faced one and others, on an auspicious lunar day, [I,] the venerable [Name], together with my wife and children, shall perform the re-establishment of the fires—the domestic fire and the others—which have been interrupted for a long time. Having cast away the *darbha* grass, having sipped water (*ācamana*), and having prepared the sacrificial mound (*sthaṇḍila*) and drawn lines: first, facing east, one should draw the lines starting from the north and ending in the south; then, facing north, one should draw the lines starting from the west and ending in the east.

Having sprinkled [the ground] with water while turning the hands downward, having cast everything away toward the southwest, having established the fire and kindled it, having swept around it, having strewn grass [around the fire] starting from the east and proceeding clockwise— placing the southern blades underneath and the northern ones on top— one sets out the seat for the vessels to the north and the seat for the vessels to the west. Having placed the curd, the ghee, the *prokṣaṇī* vessel,
and the other ladle (*darvī*), one takes up the *prokṣaṇī* vessel of that same size, fills it with water, and pours it out.

Having sprinkled all the northern vessels three times with water around the fire; having placed the strainers (*pavitra*) into the vessel for the clarified butter (*ājya*); having melted the clarified butter; having moved it toward the north; having placed them over the fire; having illuminated [the butter] with a burning blade of grass; having cut off two tips of *darbha* grass, washed them, and thrown them back into the butter; having carried the fire around them three times; having pushed the embers back toward the west; having purified the clarified butter three times by moving the strainers back and forth with their tips pointing north; having loosened the knot of the strainers; and having touched water—[he should proceed].

(…) He throws [the wooden sword] into the fire. Having heated that with which he offers in the fire, having wiped it with *darbha* grass, having heated it again, having sprinkled it, and having set aside the *darbha* grass, he touches the *darbha* grass (4th line) and throws it into the fire, saying: "Aditi, give your consent! Anumati, give your consent! Sarasvatī, give your consent! God Savitṛ, impel!
(5th line) Homage to Agni Jātavedas! Homage to Sahojas! Homage to Antirā(-)prabhu! Homage to Vaiśvānara! Homage to Naiyāpasa! (6th line) [...]

Salutation to Soma and to the pervasive one; salutation to the Person of Sacrifice; salutation to the Self; salutation to all the Śrīvaiṣṇavas. [Having taken] the principal *darbha* grasses... and with the other ladle, having taken that clarified butter: *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā; this is for Prajāpati, not mine.* *Oṃ, the expiation for Agni’s following [the oblation], and the oblation for...* (8th line).

I shall perform [it]. This [is] the navel of this... thou art made of iron; held by an iron mind, thou carriest the oblation with iron. With iron... bestow healing, svāhā! May the light of the iron-minded Agni enjoy the clarified butter; may he kindle the interrupted sacrifice. Those who... and those who revile, I join them together with this oblation... svāhā! This is for the light of the mind, not mine. Whatever defilement has occurred in my self, may Agni restore that again...

Hā! O Jātavedas, you who move among all people, Svāhā! That which belongs to Jātavedas is mine; this is not mine. Agni has given back the eye, Indra, Bṛhaspati, and the two Aśvins have restored it to the eyes, Svāhā! That which belongs to the Self is mine; this is not mine. May the Ādityas, Rudras, and Vasus unite [it] again... (5th line)...

through the guidance of the Vasus and by means of the sacrifice, increase my body according to your vow. May the desires of the sacrificer come true, Svāhā! That which belongs to the Ādityas is mine; this is not mine. (6th line)

Svāhā! To Agni, this [is mine], not mine. Om Bhuvaḥ Svāhā! To Vāyu, this [is mine], not mine. Om Suvaḥ Svāhā! To Sūrya, this [is mine], not mine. Om Bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ... To Prajāpati, this [is mine], not mine. Om! For the sake of the evening and morning oblations performed at various times, for the purpose of the name-giving rite, and as a general expiation (*sarvaprāyaścitta*), [I offer] the Soma-oblation... 8th line.

Om bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ svāhā. To Prajāpati, not to me. For the purpose of expiation for the non-performance of numerous Darśapūrṇamāsa sthālīpākas, I shall perform this expiatory oblation. Om bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ svāhā. To Prajāpati, not to me. Om, for the re-establishment of this interrupted aupāsana fire... (2nd line)

In the midst of the sacrifice, for the sake of expiation for all ritual transgressions—including errors in the application of mantras and tantras, as well as omissions, excesses, and all other violations of the prescribed rules—I shall perform the *sarvaprāyaścitta* (universal expiation), beginning with the *anājñāta* [and other] oblations. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā! This is for Prajāpati, not for me. Whatever of the sacrifice is performed incorrectly, whether unknown or known, O Agni... [of this... *(Note: The final portion of the text provided appears to be a fragment of a Vedic mantra regarding the rectification of ritual errors.)*

Do you indeed prepare [this] for him, just as it is, *svāhā*! This is for Agni, not mine. The sacrifice is commensurate with the person; the sacrifice is commensurate with the person... do you indeed prepare that for him, just as it is, *svāhā*! This is for Agni, not mine. Separately, with a mind of humble resolve, O wise one, look upon the cooked portions of the sacrifice; may Agni establish them for you.

[O] Kratu... [you have] opened the two-fold gates. What remains for the gods... svāhā! To Agni this, not mine. O Agni, you who know, may you remove from us the wrath of the god Varuṇa; as the best of sacrificers and the bearer [of oblations], being purified, release all enmities from us—svāhā! To Agni-Varuṇa this, not mine. In Agni, the powerful one, [the sacrifice] has shone forth; most near to this [earth], at the pressing, he has appeased Varuṇa; release us from the ocean [of distress], grant us mercy.

Easy to invoke, the leader in battle—*svāhā*! To Agni and Varuṇa, this [is mine], not mine. By these songs, whatever was deficient therein, O Lord of Bay Horses, increase it as you grow; when the archer... (*āstro*)... we have attained the cow-pens (*gotrā*). May the splendor (*bhrājaḥ*) be in me; then may we be yours—*svāhā*! To Indra, the Lord of Bay Horses, this [is mine], not mine. Viṣṇu strode across this; he established his foot in three places. His step is gathered together in the secret place—*svāhā*! To Viṣṇu, this [is mine], not mine. *Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā*! To Agni, this [is mine], not mine. *Oṃ suvaḥ svāhā*! To Vāyu, this [is mine], not mine.

Oṃ suva svāhā! To Vakriyya, this [is offered], not mine. Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ svāhā! To Prajāpati, this [is offered], not mine. Oṃ, for the sake of the perfection of the rite, I shall perform the *ādi-homa* to Keśava and the others. Oṃ Keśavāya svāhā! To Keśava, this [is offered], not mine. Dāmodarāya svāhā! To Dāmodara, this [is offered], not mine. Oṃ Viṣṇave svāhā! To Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self, this [is offered], not mine. Oṃ Śrīkṛṣṇāya namaḥ. (Twice, thrice). [Perform] breath control (*prāṇāyāma*) and sprinkling (*pariṣecana*). Adite, grant us permission... (8th line)

*Matenavamāsthāḥ*. *Sarasvatemanvamasthāt*. *Devasavitaḥ prāsāvīḥ*. *Oṃ*, from the beginning of the *vicchinna* [rite] up until this moment, *Oṃ* (... (P007b, 1st line). The divine *sthālīpāka* substance is offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. [Perform] *prāṇāyāma*. *Oṃ*, by the command of the Blessed Lord, as service (*kaiṅkarya*), yesterday evening (... (2nd line), together with today’s morning *aupāsana* oblation, I shall perform the *homa*. *Adite 'numanyasva prasuva*. *Catvāri śṛṅgā... viveśa*. *Eṣa hi deva* (... (3rd line).

O Agni, be present; I shall offer. Offer! Taking rice filled with twelve joints and dividing it into two portions: *oṃ agnaye svāhā*. To Agni this, not mine. *oṃ agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā*. To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt this, not mine. I shall offer. Offer! Taking the rice as before and dividing it into two portions: *oṃ sūryāya svāhā*. To Sūrya this, not mine. *agnaye sviṣṭakṛte svāhā*. To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt this, not mine.

Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā! To Agni, this, not mine. To Agni, this, not mine. Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā! To Vāyu, this, not mine. Oṃ suvaḥ svāhā! To Sūrya, this, not mine. Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-svaḥ svāhā! To Prajāpati, this, not mine. The Eye has risen; you have sent it forth. Oṃ Śrī Viṣṇave svāhā! To Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self, this, not mine. To Agni, for the sake of a good path and wealth—O God, knowing all our intentions, keep far from us every sin that binds us; we shall worship you with abundant homage. To Agni, obeisance.

O Consumer of Oblations, whatever has been offered by me—devoid of mantras, devoid of ritual action, or devoid of devotion—may that be made complete for You, O God. Among all penances without exception, those consisting of austerity and ritual acts, the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is supreme. I offer salutations; having prostrated, having sipped water, with body, speech, mind, along with the senses, intellect, and self, or even through my natural disposition, whatever I do in entirety, I dedicate it to the Supreme Śrīmannārāyaṇa.

My morning *aupāsana* fire-ritual is offered unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa. O Hali! Om! May there be auspiciousness. I shall perform the entrustment of my self into the service (*kaiṅkarya*) commanded by the Blessed Lord. O Agni, with that body of yours which is worthy of sacrifice, come here and ascend [into me]. As the Self, enter into the self; bringing many riches to this person, lead him toward them. Having become the sacrifice, O Jātavedas, go to your source; being born again, come to that dwelling. (உலப? *Ulab?* (Note: This appears to be a local or dialectal invocation).

[The Aupāsana Rite] Having washed his feet, sipped water twice, and performed breath control (*prāṇāyāma*), [he thinks: "With this my lawful wife, by the command of the Blessed Lord, I shall perform the *prāyaścitta* and the *homa*. Having touched water, having scraped [the ground], having placed water to the east, and having kindled the fire, he [addresses] the south with the words, "O Aditi, be gracious."
"O Anumati, grant your approval up to the final release; O Sarasvatī, grant your approval; O God Savitṛ, impel [the sacrifice]. Having taken the uncrumbled [grain], he recites:

"He who has four horns, three feet, two heads, and seven hands—he, the threefold-born bull, roars loudly; Mahādeva has entered into him. Having thus cast [the grain] into the fire and joined his palms in *añjali*, he recites: "For this god extends across all the quarters; for he was born, and he is within the womb, being born again."

"May he, as he is about to be born, stand facing westward, with his face turned toward all directions. O Agni, be present before me. Having thus prayed and taken unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), [he recites]:

"Oblation to Agni Jātavedas! Oblation to Apahojas! Oblation to Ajirāprabhava! Oblation to Vaiśvānara! Oblation to Naya! Oblation to Apa...! Oblation to Paṅktirādhas! ... to Visarpiṇ! Oblation to Agni! Oblation to Ātman! Oblation to all the Śrī-Vaiṣṇavas! I shall offer [this] rice grain..."

Having taken [the portion] and having divided it into two, he offers it with: "To Sūrya, svāhā! Having offered, [he assigns the remnant]: "This is for Sūrya, not mine. "To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, svāhā! "This is for Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, not mine.

"Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā! "This is for Agni, not mine. "Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā! "This is for Vāyu, not mine. "Oṃ suvaḥ svāhā! "This is for Sūrya, not mine. "Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ suvaḥ svāhā! "This is for Prajāpati, not mine. "O Aditi, you have partaken of my offering. O Anumati, you have partaken of my offering. O Sarasvatī, you have partaken of my offering."

O God Savitṛ, you have impelled [us]. Oṃ, svāhā to Śrī Viṣṇu. This is for Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self, not for me. Rising up: "O Agni, lead us by a good path to wealth... O God, knowing our ways, keep away from us the crooked sin; we shall offer to you the most abundant word of homage. Svāhā to Agni. O Consumer of Oblations, whatever has been offered by me deficient in mantra, deficient in ritual action, or deficient in devotion—may that be made complete for you, O God. All expiations and all rites... [are completed].

Indeed, among all those [duties], the remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is supreme. Having saluted and prostrated—(with body, speech, and mind)—whatever I do today, whether by nature or through my own disposition, I offer it all to the glorious Nārāyaṇa. May this evening worship be an offering unto Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Hariḥ Oṃ. For the evening time, I shall perform the evening *aupāsana* oblation (*homa*). And those two... (4th line).

When the *aupāsana* fire is extinguished, the expiatory oblation (*prāyaścittāhuti*) is as follows: *ayāścāgne 'sy anabhiśastīś ca satyamit tvamayā asi | ayāsā san munojivā havirūhiṣe ||* (Expiatory Oblation) *Yā no yehi bheṣajaṃ svāhā |* To Agni Ayas, this [is mine], not mine. To Śrī Viṣṇu, svāhā... Having washed one’s feet and sipped water twice, and having taken three blades of *darbha* grass with their tips intact as a purifier (*pavitra*), one should meditate: "May we prosper in our offerings, together with our offspring. Then, with the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*)...

Taking unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) mixed with water, [he recites]: "May these offerings to the Brahmins—which are the causes for the attainment of all prosperity, which have arisen as comets to destroy the masses of calamities, and which are like the shoreless ocean—purify me. Having thus scattered [the grains] upon the ground, he becomes *upavītin* (wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder). "Salutation to the gods (*devebhyo namaḥ*). Becoming *prācīnāvītī* (wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder), [he recites]:

"Salutation to our great-grandfathers (*asmat-mahā-prapitāmahebhyo namaḥ*). Becoming *upavītin* again, [he recites]: "Salutation to the glorious Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the Śrāddha; salutation to the deities and the ancestors, and to the Great Yogin... (Note: The ellipses indicate portions of the text omitted from the source.)

Salutations to Svadhā, salutations to Svāhā; always, salutation after salutation. Having prostrated, he makes this request: "O Lord, on this day, for [the sake of] my father, [named] Amukaśarman, I desire to perform the annual *śrāddha*. May this place and time be auspicious for me in this [performance]. May all the materials, both cooked and uncooked, being offered here, be worthy of the *śrāddha*. By the performance of this annual *śrāddha* for my father..."
"May you grant this prosperity. Response: "So be it. [The ritual action: "Let there be the form of fire... [The sacred thread: Wearing the *upavīta* facing north. At the time of the *śrāddha*:

"...having [invoked] the god Janārdana... [The sacred thread: Wearing the *prācīnāvīta* facing south. "To the Vasus and others, and to the ancestors, I shall now perform the *śrāddha*. [The ritual action: ... (P010b(7), 1st line).

Wear the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavīta*). Seated upon *darbha* grass, holding *darbha* blades, and having restrained the breaths (*prāṇāyāma*), [recite]: "To Him who wears white garments... [and] "Śrī Govinda... While this [time] is present, wear the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). On this auspicious lunar day, by the command of the Blessed Lord [for the sake of service], wear the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). Of such-and-such lineage (*gotra*) and such-and-such name (*śarman*), my father—today, on this anniversary, I shall perform the annual *śrāddha* according to the *pārvaṇa* rite. Having cast away the *darbha* grass and sipped water, [proceed].

Having drawn a line from west to east, having placed water to the east, facing south, and having touched the knees while placing the thumb and ring finger of the left hand on the ground—(5th line)—"May those ancestors who are on earth, those in the intermediate space, those in heaven, or those who are brownish beings, may they all come together at this sacrifice. Having strewn [the grass] in reverse order, with each subsequent layer to the north and each preceding layer to the south, there is a seat for the vessels to the north, a seat for the *praṇītā* water-vessel, and a seat for the vessels to the west; [and] the *darvī* ladle. (7th line)

Having lifted up the *ājyasthālī* (ghee-pot), the *prokṣaṇī* (sprinkling-vessel), and the *praṇītā* (water-vessel), and having set down the other—the *darvī* (ladle)—and the vessel for the oblation (*havirpātra*), [one should prepare] the *praṇītā* vessel to that same measure. Having filled the *prokṣaṇī* vessel with water from the [main] water-vessel, and having filled [the others] three times with water, one should sprinkle all the subsequent vessels with all the water.

Then, taking the *praṇītā* vessel and filling it with water, having purified it three times with unbroken rice (*akṣata*) and having leveled it with the breaths, [one places it] on the *darbha* grass to the north of the fire.

Having placed [the materials] down and having set the strainer (*pavitra*) into the vessel for clarified butter (*ājyapātra*), [he takes up] the sacred thread (*upavīta*). *Oṃ asmin mama pituḥ pratyābdikaśrāddhahomakarmaṇi brahmāṇam āvāhayāmi.* (I invoke the Brahman priest in this annual *śrāddha* fire-offering ritual for my father.

*brahmaṇe namaḥ* | *idam āsanam* | *idam arcanam*. *Oṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ satyaṃ tvartena pariṣiñcāmi* | *abhrāttopastaraṇam asi*. [Prāṇāyāma... *brahmaṇe svāhā* | *brahmaṇe namaḥ* | *idaṃ gulopahāraṃ nivedayāmi*. *amṛtāpitānam asi tāmbūlaṃ samarpayāmi*. (You are the drinker of nectar; I offer betel.)

I offer all the ritual services (*upacāra*). Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*), having melted the clarified butter (*ājya*), having moved the coals toward the north, having placed [the vessel] upon them, having illuminated it with a burning blade of grass, having cut off two tips of *darbha* grass, having washed them, having cast them back [into the fire], and having untied the knot of the purifier (*pavitra*), he touches water and throws [the tips] into the fire with their points directed eastward. This is the means by which he offers. (...)

Having satiated [the deities], having wiped [the ladle] with *darbha* grass, having satiated them again, having sprinkled [water], and having set down the ladle, he touches the *darbha* blades with water and casts them into the fire. He [casts] the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*)...
"I loosen... The southern half is narrower and longer; the northern [half] is smaller and more heart-like. [He wears] the sacred thread (*upavīta*). ... [He places] two fuel sticks upon his chest.

Having touched the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) with his hand, he places the southern one on top of the northern one. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*), he silently sprinkles water all around in a clockwise direction. [Then, regarding] the fuel-stick (*idhma*) in the clarified butter:

"O Brahman, in this *pratyābdika-śrāddha-homa* rite of mine, O Father, I shall place the fuel-stick. Response: "Place it. Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavīta*), while meditating upon Prajāpati, he pours the two libations (*āghāra*). He offers the other [oblation] with the *darvī* spoon, from the north-western corner to the south-eastern corner: "To Prajāpati, svāhā! To Prajāpati..."

This is not mine. Having offered [the portion] ending with Īśāna, [one says]: *indrāya svāhā*. This is for Indra, not mine. *agnaye svāhā*. This is for Agni, not mine. *somāya svāhā*. This is for Soma, not mine. *Oṃ agnaye svāhā*. This is for Agni, not mine. *Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ svāhā prajāpataye*. This is for Prajāpati, not mine. Rising and taking unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*): "O Viśvedevas of great power, you who are appointed here at this Śrāddha, may you be attentive. O Viśvedevas...

O gods, may you hear me—those who are in the intermediate space, those who are in the sky, and also those who are worthy of worship—do you all sit down immediately upon this sacrificial grass (*barhis*). This is the unbroken protection of Gotra Śarman; this is the worship. O Viśvedevas, for the sake of Gotra Śarman, you must grant your favor. Response: *Oṃ*, so be it. Request: He attains [it].

Sir, please respond. May I receive [the response]. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*), taking a sesame seed, he says: "O Soma-loving ancestors, come by the deep, ancient paths; grant us progeny, wealth, long life, and a hundred autumns. Today, at this *śrāddha*, I invoke the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather of my father, belonging to the Gotra of Śarman. I bring for the ancestors this sacrificial grass (*barhis*) that is cut in one stroke, soft as wool, and pleasant; may my Soma-like ancestors sit upon it.

Grandfathers and great-grandfathers, together with their attendants. At this annual *śrāddha* for the lineage of Śarman, this is the seat for the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. [Response: "So be it. At this *śrāddha* for the lineage of Śarman, you should grant your presence (*kṣaṇa*) for the sake of the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. [Taking unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) while reciting the *Sahasraśīrṣā* hymn, etc.,] at this *śrāddha* for the lineage of Śarman, I invoke the illustrious Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*.

The Person alone is this [universe] which grows by means of food. This seat is for Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*. This is the worship. For the sake of the *śrāddha* of [Name], of the [Gotra] lineage, for the purpose of Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, you must grant your consent (*kṣaṇa*).

Om. As before. "Carrying strength, immortality, ghee, milk, nectar, and flowing around—may there be *svadhā*; satisfy my ancestors. Let it be lifted up, and let it be offered into the fire. [Prati... *Note: The bracketed placeholders indicate that the specific name and lineage of the deceased are to be inserted.*

[The officiant] should speak these words: "Let [the portion] be lifted; let it be placed in the fire. Taking the sacrificial oblation (*havis*) and the vessel containing the oblation, he should place it to the north of the fire. Having sprinkled it over, he should offer it into the fire in the northern part. Having spread clarified butter (*ājya*) with the *darvī* spoon and having taken two portions—three portions for those who have five ancestors (*pañcārṣeya*)—and having sprinkled it once, he should recite:

"Whatever [portion] she has desired while moving according to her vows, may my father unite that seed with me. May they come together for mutual protection. To Śarmaṇa, Svāhā! To Śarmaṇa... [he continues]. Even in the sixth line, [he offers] to Śarmaṇa.

Having taken up the *mitradanna* [portion] with the ladle, having cut off two portions, and having sprinkled [clarified butter] once over them: "Those that stand, those that run, those that dwell around the fire—having pierced through the interior of the Sustainer of All, I have established the Fathers within the protection (*śarman*). To the protection, *svāhā*! To the protection from us, to the Father; this is not mine. Having spread a base [of clarified butter] in the ladle, having cut off two portions, and having sprinkled [clarified butter] once over them: "That which is mine..."
My grandmother, practicing the vows of her son, has led me astray; may my grandfather take back that seed of mine. Let another man come for my protection; *svāhā*.

(Second line) For my protection, for our grandfather—this [is his], not mine. [The ghee] is held with the ladle. I have placed a barrier between us with mountains, with the great earth, and with these infinite directions; I have placed a barrier between myself and my grandfather. *Svāhā* for protection. For my protection, for me—for the offering made with the ladle—whatever my great-grandmother, practicing the vows of her son, has led me astray, that [seed of mine... (Fourth line).

May the great-grandfather accept [this]; may another [deity] partake. To Śarman, Svāhā! To our great-grandfather Śarman, this [is offered]... (5th line) ...having poured [the ghee], having placed it within...
with the seasons, with the days and nights together with the months, with the half-months and the months, in the interval, may the great-grandfather...

*Hanāya svadhā svāhā*. To Agni Kavyavāhana, [offered] with *svadhā*; this is for him, not for me. [Then] the sacred thread (*upavīta*) is worn. One should offer [the oblation] in the north-eastern part of the fire. Having spread [a handful of] *darbha* grass, having cut off [a portion of the offering] once, and having sprinkled [clarified butter] over it twice, one says: "To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, *svāhā*. To Agni Sviṣṭakṛt, this is for him, not for me. [Then] the sacred thread is worn over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). Having spread [a base of clarified butter] in the ladle, having taken the sacrificial food, and having sprinkled [butter] over it, one says: "*Svāhā*"—thus [one offers] into the northern ashes. [This concludes] the application of the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*) and the work of smearing. [The vessel for] the clarified butter... (text fragmentary).

The principal [darbha] is on the south; the non-principal is in the middle. Taking the darbhas for placing the vessels—[using their] tip, middle, and root—in this manner three times. Placing a single darbha on his lap, he offers the remaining ones into the fire. Taking the darbha that was lying underneath, he strikes away the grass and performs the cleansing, as well as the consecration of the fire. Having wiped it on the ground, he removes the enclosing sticks (*paridhi*).

The other two [priests] offer the oblations. Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavītī*), having cast two *āghāra* fuel-sticks into the fire, they offer an oblation of clarified butter with the two ladles (*darvī*). Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*), [he offers] to the Vasus, the Rudras, and the Ādityas, who partake of the remnants of the poured butter; "this is not mine. Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavītam*): "Om! In this *pratyābdika-śrāddha-homa* rite for my father, whatever omission of mantras or omission of ritual acts may have occurred in the midst [of the performance]..."

For the sake of expiation for all ritual transgressions, whether deficient or excessive, I shall perform the *anājñāta* and other general expiatory oblations (*sarvaprāyaścitta-homa*). *Oṃ bhuvaḥ suvaḥ svāhā.* This is for Prajāpati, not for me. *Anājñātaṃ yathā jñātayajñasya kriyate mitho agne tad asya kalpayāsva; tvaṃ hi vettha yathā tathaṃ svāhā.* This is for Agni, not for me. The sacrifice is commensurate with man; the sacrifice is commensurate with man.

O Agni, fashion this for him; for you know it as it truly is. *Svāhā*! To Agni, not to me. Whatever cooked offering a mortal, through his mind, intends as a skillful act for the sacrifice—may Agni, the Hotṛ, who knows the ritual will and understands, being the best of sacrificers among the gods, offer it with the *kuśa* grass.
*Svāhā*! To Agni, not to me. Viṣṇu strode across this dusty place. *Svāhā*! (... (From P014b, line 1)

This is not mine. *Oṃ bhūḥ svāhā*. To Agni, this is not mine. *Oṃ bhuvaḥ svāhā*. To Vāyu, this is not mine. *Oṃ suvaḥ svāhā*. To Sūrya, this is not mine. (Second line) *Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ svāhā*. To Prajāpati, this is not mine. *Oṃ*, for the sake of the perfection of the rite, I shall perform the *keśava-ādi* oblation. *Oṃ keśavāya svāhā*. (Third line) To Keśava, this is not mine. *Oṃ viṣṇave paramātmane idaṃ na mama*. Having placed the vessel of clarified butter (*ājya-pātra*) to the north, [he performs] breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). [He wears the sacred thread] over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). (Fourth line)

Having silently sprinkled water around the entire perimeter in a clockwise direction; having performed the sprinkling of the *praṇītā* vessel; having filled that [vessel] with other water; having placed a little water three times each in the four directions starting from the east and in the upward direction; having placed the water remaining in the vessel to the west and then to the east; [having put on] the sacred thread (*upavīta*); having sprinkled oneself with it; [saying]: "O Brahman, I give you a boon"; "I establish the Brahman in his proper place"; "Svāhā to Śrī Viṣṇu"; "To Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self."

This is not mine. Rising, [he performs] the service. O Agni, lead [him]; the supreme remembrance of Śrī Kṛṣṇa is paramount. Having performed a prostration preceded by a salutation, with the sacred thread over the right shoulder (prācīnāvīta), facing south, and having moved the left hand [over the right], having sprinkled the oblation: "This is for you, O Tātāmara... [the] stream of Sarasvatī...

(2nd line) "...and as much as the measure of the horse, so much of this [oblation] do I give to these two. Just as Agni is inexhaustible and undecaying, so may it be inexhaustible and undecaying for my grandfather. (3rd line)

Together with the *svadhā* offerings, may you live... and this is your greatness. This honeyed wave of yours belongs to the Grandfather (*pitāmaha*), to Sarasvant, to Vāstavya, and to Vāyu and the intermediate space (*antarikṣa*).

May they protect me. To such an extent is their measure; to that same measure do I give these measures to you. Just as Vāyu is protected and not overtaken, so may it be for my Grandfather—protected and not overtaken.

May there be *svadhā* for you... *svadhā*. Together with them, may we live upon the *svadhā* in the conquered greatness. This honeyed wave of yours belongs to the Great-Grandfather (*prapitāmaha*), to Sarasvant, and to Vāstavya... (Note: The ellipses indicate portions of the text where the manuscript is damaged or illegible.)

The Āditya and as many measures as there are—so much of their measure do I grant, so that the Āditya may be inexhaustible and unfailing for me, for my great-grandfather, inexhaustible and unfailing; *svadhā*! May you live together with those who have drunk and eaten [the offerings]. The Yajus-formulas are your greatness. Having caused all to be consumed and having scattered sesame seeds, [he puts on] the sacred thread (*upavīta*).

[Reciter: "In this *śrāddha* of [Name] Śarman, this is the seat for the Viśvedevas. For the sake of the Viśvedevas, you should grant your consent (*kṣaṇa*). [Invited Guest: “Oṃ, so be it; may you receive it. (Response) “May I receive it. [Reciter: Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*): “In this *śrāddha* of [Name] Śarman of the [Gotra] lineage, this is the seat for the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. For the sake of the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, you should grant your consent. [Invited Guest: “Oṃ, so be it; may you receive it. (Response) “May I receive it. [Reciter: Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavīta*): “Of the [Gotra] lineage...”

[For] Śarman, at the *śrāddha*. O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the *śrāddha*, this is your mouth. For the sake of Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, you must grant your presence (*kṣaṇa*). (5th line) *Oṃ tathā* [so be it]. May I receive [your favor]. Washing of the feet. To the north, upon a square mandala, for [the one of] such-and-such lineage, named Śarman, at the *śrāddha*, for the Viśvedevas... today (6th line), in this place, is this seat. This is the worship (*arcana*). Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). Upon a circular mandala, for [the one of] such-and-such lineage... at the *śrāddha*, for the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather... today (7th line).

In the proper place is this seat; this is the worship; the sacred thread is placed to the north upon a square mandala. In the *śrāddha* for [Name] of the [Gotra] lineage: "In the proper place is this seat for you; this is the worship. Taking a water-pot containing rice-grains and standing facing west, [one says]: "O Viśvedevas, welcome to the *śrāddha*. [Water for] the feet: "May the divine waters be auspicious for our desire; may they be for our drinking; may they bring us peace and prosperity. [This is] the fulfillment of all success. [The scattering of] dust. The sacred thread is worn over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*).

Taking a water-pot mixed with sesame seeds, [he says] at the sacred site (*goṣṭha*): "O Father, Grandfather, and Great-grandfather, welcome! Here is water for your feet (*pādya*). *Śanno devīrabhiṣṭaye... naḥ*. (4th line) O all you gathered particles of dust! [He offers] the sacred thread (*upavīta*). Taking a water-pot with unbroken rice grains (*sākṣata*), [he says] at the sacred site: "To Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, this is your water for the feet (*pādya*). *Tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ... padam*. Having washed his feet and sipped water twice (*dvirācamya*), [he says]: "O Viśvedevas, these [are offered] for the sake of clothing, the sacred thread, the upper garment, and ornaments. (6th line)

Unbroken grains. For the purpose of adornment, these perfumes according to their respective portions; for the purpose of garlands, these flowers and *tulasī* leaves. [The deity] has been worshipped with flowers, incense, and lamps in this complete ritual service. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). O Father, Grandfather, and Great-grandfather, these sesame seeds are for the purpose of clothing, sacrificial threads, upper garments, and ornaments. For the purpose of adornment, these perfumes according to their respective portions; for the purpose of garlands, these flowers and *śrī* leaves. Perfumes and flowers.

Well-honored with incense, lamps, and all forms of worship; the sacred thread (*upavīta*). O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the *śrāddha*, these unbroken grains (*akṣata*) are for the sake of the garment, the sacrificial thread, the upper cloth, and ornaments; these perfumes (*gandha*) are for the sake of decoration according to their respective portions; these flowers and sacred *tulasī* leaves are for the sake of garlands. Well-honored with incense, lamps, and all forms of worship; purification of the site. The sacrificial thread worn over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). "Driven away... the Rakṣasas... and the Piśācas who... (5th line).

The earth consumes [the impurities]; let them go elsewhere, wherever their minds have gone. Having lifted [the water] and sprinkled it—let the lower ones rise, and let the higher ones rise. Having churned up the waters, may those Soma-loving ancestors come; may they protect us at the invocations, O fathers, with that life-force which you possess, O you who dwell in the stronghold. [Putting on the sacred thread: Whether one is impure or pure, or even if one has reached any state whatsoever, whoever remembers the Lotus-Eyed One becomes pure both internally and externally. Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ. Salutation to the glorious Nārāyaṇa.

Having sprinkled [water] thus: "This is the seat; this is the vessel" at the place of food for the Viśvedevas. ... "This is the seat; this is the vessel-seat" at the place of food for the great-grandfathers. The sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavīta*). At the place of food for Mahā-Viṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, the vessel-seat. This is the vessel-seat. The sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*). The touching of the vessels. Having taken a little of the remnants of the offered food into the vessel for the ancestors, one should recite the mantra-passages that destroy the Rākṣasas, beginning with *sādiras*.

"I shall perform [the sacrifice]. Truly, the sacrifices of both the gods and the asuras were extended; by means of the *svāhā* [exclamation], we shall go to the heavenly world. Having thus spoken, those asuras, having girded themselves, suddenly advanced. The gods, however, were like those practicing *brahmacarya* and performing austerity; they were bewildered by the asuras and did not perceive them. They became exhausted. By that [means], they went to the heavenly world. Indeed, by means of the extended sacrifice, the gods went to the heavenly world, and by the extended [sacrifice], they [excluded] the asuras.

The sacrifice indeed proceeds when one wears the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder (*yajñopavītin*); it does not proceed for one who is not so invested. Whatever a Brahmin studies, teaches, or sacrifices while wearing the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder, that very act becomes a true sacrifice for him; therefore, one should study, officiate at sacrifices, or sacrifice while wearing the sacrificial cord over the left shoulder. This constitutes the commencement of the sacrifice. Alternatively, having sat down to the south, one places the skin over the left shoulder and the right arm under it; this is called *yajñopavīta*. The reverse of this—placing the right arm over and the left under—is called *prācīnāvīta*. We protect this [sacrificial thread]... from harm.

In the *puronuvāka* [of the *haviryajña*], Prajāpati performed the *tapograha*. He extended it and addressed them with a boon. Regarding those [rites] beginning with the unled (*apraṇīta*) and ending with the *uddhā*—Prajāpati said to them: "Fight! Fight! Therefore, as one rises, [one thinks: "I fight against the *rakṣas* until the sun sets. Indeed, these *rakṣas* are here in the pits; they are driven away by [water] consecrated with the *gāyatrī*. Thus, these exponents of the Veda (*brahmavādinaḥ*), facing the east, perform the twilight worship (*saṃdhyā*).
The waters consecrated by the *gāyatrī* which they scatter upwards—these waters, having become thunderbolts (*vajra*), cast those *rakṣas* and *mandehas* into the abyss.

By walking clockwise, he shakes off evil. Meditating upon the sun as it rises and as it sets, performing [the rites]... knowing [this], the wise man attains complete auspiciousness. "That sun is Brahman"—being Brahman itself, he who knows this reaches Brahman. Immediately thereafter, O Brahman, for the sake of the *bheraṣṭra*... the Brahmin...

[He becomes] no [longer] a Brahmin; he indeed acquires spiritual luster (*brahmavarcasa*). [He wears] the sacred thread (*upavīta*). "Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ! We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine Savitṛ; may he impel our thoughts. Having offered pure water with the words, "O divine Savitṛ, you have impelled [this]," [he says]: "The earth is your vessel, the sky is your lid. I offer you into the mouth of Brahman; I offer you into the out-breath and in-breath of the Brahmins. You are my eye; do not fail as my eye in yonder world, O so-and-so! "Viṣṇu strode across this [universe]."

He has placed his foot in three ways; it is gathered within the essence of the waters. O Viṣṇu, protect this auspicious one... [of] the Gotra and Śarman. At the annual *śrāddha*, the Viśvedevas are the deities. May this oblation (*havya*), together with its side-dishes and accompaniments, be for the Brāhmaṇa as the *āhavanīya* fire. That is the Saṃgeya-paṃ. Bhūḥ! Gadādhara is the eater of the oblation.

I am the Brahmā and the eater; the Brahmā and the eater are Brahman. The vessel is made of gold; the tree is the imperishable banyan (*akṣaya-vaṭa*). [May there be] shade at Gayā and in the city of Śrīraṅga.

It is offered at the feet of Śrī Raṅgarāja. As is convenient, [perform] the sprinkling (*pariṣecana*). Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvīta*), facing south, and bending the left knee, [recite]: *bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ*—O Viṣṇu, protect this *kavya*, the nectar.

In the *śrāddha* of the [paternal] lineage, the deities are the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather. This *kavya*, along with its side dishes and accompaniments, is for the Brāhmaṇa; however, that [portion] is for the purpose of the *āhavanīya* fire.
I declare: O Gadādhara, you were the eater of the *kavya* and the Brahman. A silver vessel was offered at Gayā, beneath the shade of the *vaṭa* tree at Akṣa, in the city of Śrīraṅga...
at the feet of Raṅgarāja. As is convenient, [there is] the ritual sprinkling (*pariṣecana*), the sacred thread (*upavīta*). *Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā*. O Viṣṇu, protect the food...

Having offered [the water] while reciting "trasya," [one says]: "O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the *śrāddha*, this food with its side-dishes is for you; O Gadādhara, you are the eater of the food, I am Brahman, and Brahman is I... Having offered the fuel-stick... all... svarga, svāhā! Bhūḥ svāhā! Bhuvaḥ svāhā! Suvaḥ svāhā! Oṃ bhūr-bhuvaḥ-suvaḥ svāhā! Aditi, give your consent; he has performed [the rite].
O Agni, by that splendor (*tejas*) which is yours, may I become splendid. By that radiance (*varcas*) which is yours, O Agni, may I become radiant. By that [power] which is yours, O Agni..."

May I become a possessor of splendor through that splendor. May Agni bestow upon me wisdom, upon me progeny, and upon me brilliance. May Indra bestow upon me wisdom, upon me progeny, and upon me power (*indriya*). May Sūrya bestow upon me wisdom, upon me progeny, and upon me radiance. To Agni... the supreme delight. I offer my salutation. Ola!
[The Five Products of the Cow].

The service of the command of the Blessed Lord: "Now I shall perform the consumption of the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*) for the purification of the body of the patron (*yajamāna*). [In the Gāyatrī: *Gomūtram* (cow-urine). *Gandhadvārā*—the cow-dung. *Āpyāyasva*—the milk. *Dadhikrāvṇo*—the curd. *Śukramasi*—the clarified butter (*ājya*). *Devasya tvā*—pure water. *Tryambakam*—churning. *Vastvagastigatam*—the straining cloth. *Tatsavitur*... [fifth line]

We meditate upon that most excellent splendor of the divine; may it inspire our intellects so that they may bring forth wisdom. I invoke Śrī, who has the fragrance as her gate, who is invincible, who bestows nourishment, who moves through the rays of light, and who is the life-force of all beings. O Soma, swell yourself on all sides when you are prepared; become the source of strength in the gathering of power.
Dadhikrāvan has performed his work for the victorious steed; he has made the mouth of the swift racer fragrant. He has extended the vital breaths... [and so forth].
*Śak*. You are semen; you are light; you are splendor. At the impulse of the god Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins and the hands of Pūṣan, I take [you].

(3rd line) We worship Tryambaka, the fragrant, the increaser of prosperity. Like a cucumber from its stem, may I be released from death but not from immortality. Whatever sin resides in my body, down to the skin and bones—by consuming the five products of the cow (*pañcagavya*), it shall be destroyed like fire by wind. (P27b[24a], 1st line)
[The Saṅkalpa Śrāddha]

Having washed his feet and taken unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*), he recites: "May we prosper through oblations, having approached with reverence; may there be friendship with the gods. Increasing our prosperity with this oblation, may we live a hundred autumns with all our heroes. Then: "Hari! Om! May those who are the causes for the attainment of all perfections, who have arisen as comets to the lineage of the wicked, and who [cross] the shoreless ocean of *saṃsāra*... may the Brahman-purifiers purify me."
Dapāṃsavaḥ! O God, salutation to the gods! Salutation to our fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers! Salutation to Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the Śrāddha!

(5th line) Having thus performed the worship... to those ancestors and to the great yogis; salutation, *svadhā*, and self-salutation—eternally, salutation after salutation! Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*): O Master, on this day, for the sake of my father, I shall perform the annual Śrāddha... (P28a, 1st line)

The place, time, recipient, and so forth have been established in this [rite]. Beholding all these objects prepared for the *śrāddha*, [one should pray]: "May there be the perfection of my qualification for performing the *śrāddha*; please grant your grace. The response is: "May there be the perfection of your qualification; may you be worthy of the *śrāddha*. [The performer] faces the north, wears the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavītin*), and at the time of the *śrāddha*, having meditated upon Gayā and the god Janārdana, and having meditated upon the ancestors beginning with the father, he then performs the *śrāddha*.

[The mantra] proceeds: "Thus [it is] facing south. "Proceed," is the reply. [He becomes] wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavītin*). He performs breath control (*prāṇāyāma*). [He makes] the formal resolve (*saṃkalpa*)—[he who is] clad in white garments, whose [attendants] have the faces of elephants and so forth. *Oṃ Śrī Govinda Govinda*, of this Blessed One, the Great Person (*mahāpuruṣa*). [He becomes] wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*). On this auspicious lunar day, [this is] service in obedience to the command of the Blessed One: today, by means of the procedure of formal resolve, the annual *śrāddha* for my father, [named] Śarman, of the [such-and-such] lineage.

"I shall do so. [Having said this,] touching water, taking a *darbha* blade, and performing the selection of the seat: "This is the seat for the Viśvedevas; it is a comfortable seat. The response is: "O [Name], of the [Gotra] lineage, for me today at this annual *śrāddha*, for the sake of the Viśvedevas known as Purūravas and Diva, you should grant the favor of being present. The response is: "Om, so be it. Having said, "May you be seated," the recipient says, "May I be seated."

With the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*): This is the seat for my father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, who are of the [name] *gotra*, [name] *śarman*, and whose natures are those of the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas.

At this annual *śrāddha* today, may you, O fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers whose natures are those of the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, grant me your presence. The response: [Obligation accepted].

Oṃ, so be it. May the performer (*kartā*) obtain [merit] through you; may the enjoyer (*bhoktā*) obtain [merit]. O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the *śrāddha*, this is your seat. O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the *śrāddha*, for the sake of the *śrāddha* today—[for the sake of] the father of such-and-such lineage and such-and-such name, in this annual *śrāddha*—you should grant your presence (*kṣaṇa*). Oṃ, so be it; may he obtain [merit]; may I obtain [merit]. Now, the washing of the feet: O [name], of such-and-such lineage, of such-and-such name, father, on this occasion of the annual *śrāddha*.
As in the case of Purūravas and others... [the] Viśvedevas... welcome... let there be water for the feet (*pādya*). "Let there be water for the feet," is the response here.

Having placed sesame seeds in the water for the washing of the feet, [one says]: "O father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, who are the embodiments of the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, in this annual *śrāddha* today, welcome! Let this water for the feet be yours. "Let there be water for the feet," is the response. Having cast unbroken rice grains (*akṣata*) into the water... [the] cow...

"O Śrī Mahā-Viṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, may this water for washing the feet (*pādya*) be offered today at this annual *śrāddha* for [the name of] the deceased father, Trasya Śarman. [The response: "It is water for washing the feet (*pādya*). [The performer], having likewise washed his own feet and sipped water (*ācamana*), performs the invocation (*āvāhana*). "O gods known as Purūravas and the others, I shall invoke you; please come. [The response: "Invoke them. "O Viśvedevas, you have come; hear this oblation... (3rd line)

O Viśvedevas, hear this [invocation]—you who are in the intermediate space, you who dwell in heaven, you whose tongue is Agni, O worshipful ones... (4th line) ...sit upon this sacred grass (*barhis*). Today, at this annual *śrāddha* for my father, the protector of the *gotra*, I invoke the Viśvedevas known by the names of Purūravas and the others.
(5th line) Invoke them! May the illustrious and mighty Viśvedevas come; those who are appointed here to this *śrāddha*, may they be attentive. (6th line)

May they be present for you. Today, at this annual *śrāddha* ceremony for my father, [named] Śarman, of the [such-and-such] lineage, this is the seat for the Viśvedevas known as Purūravas and the others. It is a comfortable seat. For the sake of the Viśvedevas, [accept] the invitation (*ākṣaṇa*). Oṃ, may it be so; may you receive it, and may I receive it from you. [The performer], wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*), takes sesame seeds and says: "For my father, [named] Śarman, of the [such-and-such] lineage, at this annual *śrāddha*, [I invoke] the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers, who are of the nature of the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas."
I shall invoke you among yourselves. Invoke! ... we meditate upon your forms; desiring you, we meditate upon you. Desiring [us], bring the ancestors here for the oblation...

of the *gotra* of Śarman, in this annual *śrāddha*, I invoke the ancestors—father, grandfather, and great-grandfather—who are of the nature of Vasu, Rudra, and Āditya. Come, O gentle ancestors, along with the Agniṣvātta gods by the paths traveled by the deities; at this sacrifice, [partake] with the *svadhā* offering.

[May they] not [be] intoxicated... let them speak for me; may they protect us... of the *gotra* of Śarman, my father—today, at this annual *śrāddha*, this is the seat for the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers, who are the very forms of Vasu, Rudra, and Āditya. O fathers, grandfather, and great-grandfather... you should grant your consent. Om, so be it. You have received [the invitation]; I have received it. I shall invoke the venerable Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, among you. Invoke him!

The thousand-headed Puruṣa... [for] my father Śarman, today at this annual śrāddha, O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the śrāddha: this is your seat. For the sake of Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the śrāddha, you should grant your consent. Om, so be it; may you accept it. May I accept it. [For] ornaments: O Viśvedevas... these unhusked grains (akṣata) are for the purpose of upper garments and jewelry. For the purpose of adornment... [etc. (6th line).

Just as these fragrances are for the respective portions: garlands, [fragrant substances], and sacred *tulasī* leaves; well-honored with all offerings such as perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and so forth; these unbroken grains (*akṣata*) are for the sake of clothing, the sacred thread (*yajñopavīta*), the upper garment (*uttarīya*), and ornaments for the venerable protector of the *śrāddha*;

these are for the purpose of decoration; these are your perfumes for the purpose of [anointing]; these flowers and sacred *tulasī* leaves are for the purpose of worship; these two *darbha* grasses are for the purpose of purification.

Having worshipped with all offerings such as perfumes, flowers, incense, lamps, and so forth, one takes a blade of *darbha* grass at the place of eating and recites: "Driven away are the Rakṣasas, the Piśācas; those who dwell upon the earth, let them go to the bottomless abyss. Having removed the *darbha* grass and sprinkled water, one recites: "O sesame seeds, arise! ... they have been cast away. Having released [the bonds], may the gentle Pitṛs come today; may they protect us from envy."

In the *rohava* [mantras]: "Whether impure or pure, even if one has reached any state whatsoever, he who performs [the rite]... svāhā. Having scattered sesame seeds in the place of the ancestors (*pitṛsthāna*), having performed the purification of the ground, and having provided the eating vessels, [one says for the Viśvedevas]: "This is the seat; this is the vessel-seat. [For the ancestors: "This is the seat for the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather."

This is the seat for the vessel; this is the seat for the bowl. O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the *śrāddha*, this is the seat for the place of eating; this is the seat for the bowl. Having prepared the vessel with ghee, having offered the food and other items, and having smelled [the offering], I shall perform the recitation of the supreme mantra for the purpose of removing defects: "The head of heaven... Vaiśvānara, Agni born of the earth, the sovereign king, Aditi, whom the people call... (P32a, 1st line).

The gods produce the vessel; drive forth that which is uncooked within the raw. Make it rise to the sun in heaven, like the *gharma* heated by fervor through well-formed chants, acceptable to the great host of gods. For the sake of cooking, the milch-cow is led forth; the skillful-handed milker [drinks] from her with his heart. She is the most excellent sacrifice... she has spread out. That cow, having been milked, has yielded the *gharma*; I have proclaimed it well. Making the sound "hiṃ" as it were, desiring the calf of the Vasus in her mind, she has approached.

May [the offering] for the Aśvins increase for great good fortune; may the self-receptacles of Indra become [full]. For the sacrifice, let there be alms for the singer and his friends. May the mortal who is evil-minded, of wicked intent, and a malicious enemy, be struck down by your [missile]; may there be security. O you who possess quivers, who are well-armed, and full of arrows—[protect us] from harm! Svāhā! With the *surā* [liquor], Svāhā to Agni, the mother! Svāhā...!

The one with four locks of hair, moving about, well-anointed with ghee, has entered the pathways; he, the wise one, has established the gods in their allotted portions. That single-winged bird has entered the ocean;
he gazes upon the world. With a simple mind they behold him; O Mother, save him, save him from the mother! The wise sages call him the fair-winged one.
They conceive of him, who is one, as many through the waters; they fashion the meters from him at the sacrifices, and the twelve cups of the hymn for its measurement.

He whose praise is perfected, the great upholder of dharma—that very desire of his, the son of strength, has indeed shattered the mountain. O sweet one, we take refuge in you... be well-disposed toward us. O Father, come hither with your auspicious protections; be a source of bliss for me.

To those [who are] friends, well-disposed, free from duplicity, who dwell among the lords of the Asuras, who possess splendor as if in heaven, O Father, you give to them, or you abide with them, O Father. Like the necks of horses, they stretch themselves out toward the juices. Where, O Father, has the mind of the great gods been placed? What was done by the beautiful banner? For you have slain [the enemy] with your mind. Since you have come, O Father, thirsty for the joints... (Note: The provided text fragments are highly fragmentary and contain numerous lacunae; this translation reflects the extant portions as best as possible within the constraints of the classical context.)

May those [plants] that are our remedies come to us for our protection. Whatever portion of the waters and the plants we consume, O Vātāpi, become as food for us. O Soma, whatever parts of the cow you have withheld, may we partake of the head.
Become a nourisher of the plants; O plant, become a protector against the wolf. O Vātāpi, become food for us. Thus, O Father, we [invoke] thee... the offerings for the cow.

Having recited the *Annasūkta* beginning with "suṣira... devebhya vāsadhamā... rma... bhyaṃ tvāsadama... and having placed [the offerings] such as [water] into all the food vessels, he sprinkles them with the *Gāyatrī*: "oṃ bhūrbhuvassuvaḥ tatsaviturvareṇyam," and consecrates them with "devasavitu prasuva. Having given pure water into his hand, he [offers] with the *kūrca* [grass-bundle]: "The earth is the vessel, the sky is the lid; I place you in the mouth of the Brāhmaṇas."

"I offer. I offer you into the out-breath and in-breath of the Brahmins. May you not diminish my essence; may you prosper here and in the world of Viṣṇu over there. Having thus offered the food and other items, [one says]: "By the mantra *idaṃ viṣṇurvicakrame*, Svāhā! O Viṣṇu, protect the offering (*havya*).
At this annual *śrāddha* today, for me, the son of Gotra Śarman, the deities are the Viśvedevas known as Purūravas and others."

"This offering—food with its condiments and accompaniments, as well as I myself, who am Brahmā and the eater—is given upon the feet of Śrī Raṅganātha in the city of Śrī Raṅgam, within the shade of the imperishable banyan tree, in a golden vessel. Having thus performed the ritual of the sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*), he thereafter performs it for the ancestors. Having performed everything as before, [he recites]:

"Viṣṇu strode across this; in the dust of his footprint, *svadhā*. O Viṣṇu, protect the ancestral offering (*kavya*). [This is for] the annual *śrāddha* of [the deceased] belonging to the [such-and-such] lineage and named Śarman.

Having offered all this *kavya*—the deities being the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers in the form of the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas—in the same manner as before; and having likewise performed for Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, as before—with this distinction: [for] Mahāviṣṇu [this portion]... this food here... that which is being given... the food [offered] to Brahmā... having treated it like the *Viśvedevas*; and having performed the sprinkling (*pariṣecana*) for all.

Having performed [the ritual] thus, one should place three *darbha* blades facing south. With one [blade], Viṣṇu, the Great Being, having separately established them manifoldly, partakes [of the offering] as the All-Eater (*Viśvabhuk*). By this worship of the Śrī-Vaiṣṇava, may the Blessed Lord Janārdana—who is the very embodiment of the Viśvedevas, who is the embodiment of the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather, who is the embodiment of Śrī Mahāviṣṇu the protector of the *śrāddha*, and who is the Blessed Lord—be pleased. Gayā-śrāddha, Gayā-śrāddha.

"O imperishable banyan tree, O imperishable banyan tree! May it be nectar for the Viśvedevas. You are the spreading of nectar. Thus [he says] for the ancestors and Viṣṇu. "May everything here become nectar. You are the spreading of nectar. Svāhā! Having uttered the *svāhā* call for the out-breath (*prāṇa*), saying, "Entering through the out-breath during the *śrāddha*, I offer nectar; svāhā to the out-breath," and likewise for the downward breath (*apāna*), the pervasive breath (*vyāna*), the upward breath (*udāna*), and the equalizing breath (*samāna*), and having also uttered [the names of the deities] in the middle intervals, he then says: "Svāhā to Brahman."

[Recite] "Brahmaṇi mātmā amṛtatvāya" and "Svastinaḥ. [Recite] the Rakṣoghna hymns, the Pitṛ... [hymns], and the Pitṛ-sūktas while you are eating. I shall recite the Itihāsas and Purāṇas according to my ability. The response is: "Please recite. Having requested, "May you grant me the grace of [the holy water] from the sacred ford," and "May you grant me the nectar," the recitation follows immediately thereafter. At the time of the masters' rising, one should sing the Gāyatrī, the Ānarāpavamāna, and the [hymns beginning with] "Iyannavo..."
On the side of the gods, indeed, [is] the one who overcomes hunger and thirst; the Atharvans have directed [it] toward the gods, the god-seeking ones.

(5th line) He purifies himself at the gathering of the cows, and no one harms him. The one who bestows the plants... for the sake of the well-being of the pressed juice, for the ruddy one, for the one who acts with wisdom.

For Soma, the master of the pure [waters], the pressed juice is offered to the one who seeks the light. Let the pressed, the presser, purify the pressed Soma, [endowed] with honeyed sweetness. (P35b(32a), 1st line)

[Having formed a ball of food] with the [mantra] "svāduṣaṃsadaḥ pitaro... and having offered it, the response is: "May everything be complete... [and reciting] "madhu vātā ṛtāyate" (The winds are honey-sweet for the one who follows the cosmic order), [he says] "may our cows be honey-sweet;

honey, honey, honey. Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavītin*): "O Viśvedevas, honey! Honey has been prepared; may it be well-prepared. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītin*):

"O Viśvedevas, satisfied! We are satisfied. [Reciting] "akṣann amīmadanta... (They have eaten, they have rejoiced...), "these [priests], your dear ones, have stirred [the offerings]; the self-luminous inspired ones have praised [you]."

The objects of perception are not the mind. Those [who... perceive... the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers: "Honey! Honey! May it be well-prepared; may it be well-prepared. O fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers:
you are satisfied, we are satisfied. O Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, protector of the *śrāddha*: "Honey! Honey! May it be well-prepared; may it be well-prepared. O Śrī [protector of the *śrāddha*]...

"O Mahāviṣṇu, you are satisfied; I am satisfied. Having loosened the three *darbha* blades [and sprinkled them], and having performed the ritual purification (*mārjana*) with sesame seeds and water, he takes up the *vāyasa-piṇḍa*. "Those born in my lineage who have been cremated by fire and those who have not been cremated by fire—may they attain the supreme goal through this *piṇḍa* offered upon the earth."

"To those burnt by fire... [and] to those not burnt by fire, born of our lineage, who have died—this *piṇḍa*, *svadhā*, obeisance! May both those burnt by fire and those not burnt by fire purify themselves.

(Third line) Having performed the purification with water and sesame seeds (*tilodaka*) using the right hand, and having given the subsequent water for rinsing (*uttarāpośana*), [one says] "You are called the nectar" (*amṛtābhidhānamasi*) for all of them. Immediately thereafter, having given the *piṇḍa* for the crows (*vāyasapiṇḍa*) to the crows, and having given water for washing the feet, mouth-rinsing, and sipping to the eater and the performer, and having set aside the vessel for the remnants, [one offers] a *tulasī* leaf. (Fifth line)

He gives betel-leaf together with a sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). "This betel-leaf and sacrificial fee belong to [Name] of [Gotra] Śarman. This is your sacrificial fee. Wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*): "This betel-leaf and sacrificial fee belong to the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather of [Name] of [Gotra] Śarman. This is your sacrificial fee. The response of all is: "May there be betel-leaf. Wearing the sacred thread over the left shoulder (*upavītī*): "To [Name] of [Gotra] Śarman, the illustrious Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*, this..."
[Offer] betel. May there be betel. This is your sacrificial fee (*dakṣiṇā*). Homage to the gods. Homage to the fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers.

(Line 3) Homage to Śrī Mahāviṣṇu, the protector of the *śrāddha*. Prostration. Homage to the deities, to the ancestors, and to the great yogis; homage to Svadhā, to Svāhā, [and to the ancestors... homage again and again. On this day, for my father..., the annual *śrāddha* has been performed by me according to the scriptures... (Line 5)

May this [rite] performed at Gayā, which yields the fruit of the *śrāddha* and brings about inexhaustible satisfaction, be [accomplished] through the grace of the Blessed One (*bhagavat*)... may it be as stated [in the scriptures].

May the attainment of the fruit of the *śrāddha* be according to the *śāstra*; may there be inexhaustible satisfaction. What shall be done with the remnants of the food? Let it be eaten together with those who are dear. May our donors increase, and may the Vedas and our lineage flourish. May our *śrāddhas* not be interrupted, and may there be abundant wealth. And may there be food for us.

May there be much; may we obtain guests; and may those who ask come to us—may [the rest] not [be lacking]. The Response: May you be ours... (3rd line) ...and the Vedas indeed. May faith not depart from you, and may there be much to give, and may there be much for you... may you obtain guests. (4th line) And like those who ask... as with Māyā and Ciśyakaṃca. Om! Let the *svadhā* be uttered. ...the assembly of the Fathers, the givers of water. (5th line)
Resorting to the command, the profound ones are spoken with power; the heroes of wondrous speed and great strength, the destroyers of hosts.

By the sacred word (*brahman*), those Fathers are gentle; may the auspicious, tireless Earth protect us from misfortune. Pūṣan protects [us] from evil. He wears golden armor, the foremost leader; the Vasus are harnessed with cattle and have been sent forth. And he who... (2nd line).

May the arrows be discharged for protection; Om, having offered unbroken rice (*akṣata*). Eight by eight for the prosperity and success of all; may we prosper through the oblation and through salutation. (Third line) May it be ever new. This [woman] is auspicious. Having taken the unbroken rice, and having taken [the materials] for the sake of Śrī... wearing the sacred thread over the right shoulder (*prācīnāvītī*).
(Fourth line) Arise, O fathers, grandfathers, and great-grandfathers, together with the Viśvedevas. [Having performed the] circumambulation... (Fifth line)
The wise and policy-knowing Vājins became [his] leaders in the assemblies. His... two fathers... may he traverse the three... the path of the gods...

(6th line) "By the giving of leaf-vegetables and such, you have been subjected to such hardship; that accumulation of suffering... having expanded [the merit], [this is] the supreme among all penances (prāyaścitta). By body and speech, the annual Śrāddha for the father is offered to Śrī Kṛṣṇa. Having performed the Brahma-yajña in the interval... (2nd line)
He partakes of food together with those he desires.
[The mental resolve.]

Clad in white garments (... I, who am impure, today—by the grace of the Blessed One, the Great Person, the Primordial Viṣṇu, the Primordial Nārāyaṇa, through his immeasurable power—amidst a surging flood of great waters, wandering among many tens of millions of...
(one of them), in this vast [universe] enveloped by the coverings of earth, water, fire, air, ether, ego, the Great Principle (Mahat), and the Unmanifest (Avyakta)... (fourth line).

Within the casket of the cosmic egg (*brahmāṇḍa*), it is supported by the foundational power (*ādhāraśakti*) and the [serpents] Kūrma, Varāha, Ananta, Puṇḍarīka, Vāmana, Kumuda, Añjana, and Supratīka—the eight elephants of the directions. Upon this is established the sevenfold world-system (*saptaloka*), consisting of Atala, Vitala, Sutala, Rasātala, Mahātala, [Pātāla], and [Bhūloka].
